## Overview

Enable Gemma 4 image-prefix attention in the opt-in `ROCM_SEGMENTED_ATTN` backend, including BF16/FP8 KV cache and multiple images.

**Stack dependency: #62666 must merge first.** This branch contains the D=512 parent plus three MM commits. [Review the MM-only diff](https://github.com/big-yellow-duck/vllm/compare/ceaae9657fc6d13c86e329810ba4f641842b0adc...8c620ea4a2577c4bf2d870473d7ecee88e2fd5ea) against parent `ceaae9657f`. Targets `main` and temporarily includes the parent changes; it needs rebasing after #62666 merges.

## Claims

- Apply bidirectional attention within each image range, respecting Gemma's sliding-window clamping and preserving gaps between separate images.
- Widen native KV traversal before split partitioning so reopened past/future image keys reach the kernel; preserve MM masks in the unified fallback.
- Extend the parent's typed `segmented_attention_config.py` with image-aware selection and separately keyed optional startup tuning. Automatic backend selection remains unchanged.

## Validation

Kernel/host validation on **one Radeon AI PRO R9700 (gfx1201)**, ROCm 10 runtime (`torch 2.13.0+rocm10.0.0`) and compiled extensions:

| Check | Result |
| --- | ---: |
| Focused MM numerical cases | **40 passed** |
| Existing segmented-attention cases | **126 passed** |
| Host metadata/cache/range cases | **9 passed** |
| Repository pre-commit, including mypy | **Passed** |

The MM cases cover BF16/FP8 KV, D=64/128/256/512, GQA, ragged and zero-query rows, clamped/unclamped windows, separate/overlapping image islands, split reduction, FP8 D=512 graph replay with changed image ranges, single-query routing and softcap fallback. Host tests use real metadata construction and persistent tuning records. The focused coverage lives in existing attention suites; developer benchmarks and the separate policy-test module are excluded.

<details>
<summary>Test commands</summary>

Run from the PR checkout in a compatible ROCm environment; `ROCR_VISIBLE_DEVICES` was unset.

```bash
HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1 .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \
    tests/kernels/attention/test_segmented_attention.py -k segmented_mm

HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1 .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \
    tests/kernels/attention/test_segmented_attention.py -k 'not segmented_mm'

HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1 .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \
    tests/v1/attention/test_mm_prefix.py \
    -k 'segmented_mm or matches_range_scan or ranges_beyond_scheduled or buffer_reuse or returns_none_when_no_range'
```

</details>

### ChartQA accuracy

Full **2,500-question ChartQA test set per model/backend**, using official `lm-eval==0.4.12` relaxed accuracy. Setup: Radeon AI PRO R9700 (gfx1201), TP1, FP8 weights/KV cache, BF16 activations, batch size 8, greedy generation, 8,192-token context and 4,096-token output cap. Segmented startup autotuning was disabled.

| Model | `TRITON_ATTN` | `ROCM_SEGMENTED_ATTN` |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| [Gemma 4 12B FP8](https://huggingface.co/RedHatAI/gemma-4-12B-it-FP8-Dynamic/tree/2083adceb2a3df0465e6021e08a7196d21dbbb44) | **80.12%** | **80.68%** |
| [Gemma 4 26B-A4B FP8](https://huggingface.co/RedHatAI/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it-FP8-dynamic/tree/ed35d7abe5d940da41b4ff06eb482feb0be8cb44) | **81.00%** | **81.12%** |

**No observed ChartQA accuracy regression with `ROCM_SEGMENTED_ATTN`.** All questions, including capped answers, remain in each score's denominator.

Historical end-to-end checks at `b7c58caf76` (before the upstream sync) passed **100/100 candidate smoke checks**, alongside 50/50 earlier-MM baseline checks. These used pinned Red Hat Gemma 4 12B / 26B-A4B FP8 checkpoints, BF16 activations, BF16/FP8 KV cache and TP1, with one/two images, cached history, chunked image input, mixed image/text batches, optional tuning and 12B MTP (with nonzero accepted draft tokens). Those historical checks are serving smoke tests; the fresh rebased-source ChartQA comparison is reported above. No new serving-performance claim is made here.

## Details

Image ranges are propagated through backend metadata using the existing shared range utility. Finished image prefixes are filtered using CPU prefill metadata, so causal text/decode can reuse the text path. The main execution path adds no GPU tensor scalar reads; tuning remains a startup operation. Shared Triton helper/fallback fixes are exercised by the numerical fallback and existing segmented cases. No scheduler or model-runner changes remain in the MM-only diff.

The extra host logic is primarily backend-local image-profile selection, cache isolation and bounded tuning reuse. Image span/range count distinguish MM records from causal text records. Static selection works without startup tuning; tuning can increase first-start cost.

Usage is documented in [Attention Backend Feature Support](https://github.com/big-yellow-duck/vllm/blob/edc90a09d0ed182743becd93edc5720237a8c9a4/docs/design/attention_backends.md#rocm-segmented-attention):

```bash
vllm serve RedHatAI/gemma-4-12B-it-FP8-Dynamic \
    --dtype bfloat16 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
    --max-model-len 8192 --max-num-batched-tokens 4096 \
    --attention-backend ROCM_SEGMENTED_ATTN
```

Optional tuning: `--kernel-config '{"enable_rocm_segmented_attn_autotune":true}'`. FP8 KV retains the parent's gfx12 restriction. RDNA GPU coverage is local; CI on NVIDIA/MI300 cannot exercise these native RDNA kernels. Existing attention CI selects the host suite, while the RDNA numerical runs above provide hardware-specific validation. Validation reused existing compiled extensions. A clean wheel rebuild and quality coverage beyond single-image ChartQA remain additional validation.

Duplicate-work check: no existing PR from this head or an identical segmented-MM enablement was found. #60317 optimizes unified Triton attention; #63383 adds a separate gfx1151 HIP backend. This extends the existing segmented Triton backend on top of #62666.

AI assistance was used for implementation, validation analysis, documentation and this PR. The human submitter remains responsible for review and validation.

- [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.

- [x] **Design Fit:** Reuses the existing backend, shared mask helpers and typed config module; optional MM tuning complexity is described above.
- [x] **Testing and Validation:** Numerical and host coverage passes locally; full ChartQA comparison completed; RDNA CI and build limitations are documented.
- [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Repository hooks pass; rendered usage docs and existing attention suites are updated.
- [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Dependency, MM-only comparison, results, commands and limitations are documented.
</details>

+def segmented_query_capacity(max_query_len: int) -> int:
+    """Round a supported query length to its compiled power-of-two capacity."""
+    if not 1 <= max_query_len <= MAX_QUERY_LEN:
+        raise ValueError(f"Query length must be in [1, {MAX_QUERY_LEN}]")
+    return 1 << (max_query_len - 1).bit_length()

+def segmented_mm_prefix_bucket(span: int, ranges: int) -> tuple[int, int]:
+    """Bound image span and range-loop work without inspecting device tensors."""
+    if span <= 0 or ranges <= 0:
+        return 0, 0
+    span_bucket = next((s for s in MM_PREFIX_SPAN_BUCKETS if s >= span), span)
+    return span_bucket, 1 << (ranges - 1).bit_length()
+

+def segmented_attention_span(
+    max_seq_len: int,
+    max_query_len: int,
+    sliding_window: int,
+    mm_prefix_mode: MMPrefixMode = "none",
+    mm_prefix_max_span: int = 0,
+) -> int:
+    """Bound the visited KV span, including reopened past and future image keys."""
+    if sliding_window < 0:
+        return max_seq_len
+    if mm_prefix_mode == "none":
+        return min(max_seq_len, sliding_window + max_query_len)
+    if mm_prefix_max_span <= 0:
+        return max_seq_len
+    future = mm_prefix_max_span - 1
+    past = sliding_window
+    if mm_prefix_mode == "unclamped":
+        past = max(past, future)
+    return min(max_seq_len, max_query_len + past + future)
+
+
+def _query_capacity_buckets() -> tuple[int, ...]:
+    return tuple(1 << exponent for exponent in range(MAX_QUERY_LEN.bit_length()))

+def _long_extend_splits(
+    base_splits: int,
+    batch: int,
+    query_len: int,
+    seq_len: int,
+    hq: int,
+    hk: int,
+    dim: int,
+    bm: int,
+    *,
+    fp8: bool = False,
+) -> int:
+    """Add long-prefix parallelism while bounding the extra split workspace."""
+    if seq_len < 32768:
+        return base_splits
+    scratch_per_split = batch * segmented_query_capacity(query_len) * hq * (dim + 1) * 4
+    scratch_limit = MAX_LONG_EXTEND_WORKSPACE_BYTES * dim // 128
+    scratch_splits = scratch_limit // scratch_per_split
+    scratch_cap = 1 << (scratch_splits.bit_length() - 1) if scratch_splits else 1
+    if dim == 512 and hq // hk == 8:
+        cache_target = (16 if fp8 else 32) * 1024**2
+        kv_bytes = 2 * batch * hk * seq_len * dim * (1 if fp8 else 2)
+        cache_splits: int = triton.next_power_of_2(triton.cdiv(kv_bytes, cache_target))
+        if fp8:
+            cache_splits = max(4, cache_splits)
+        elif kv_bytes <= 64 * 1024**2:
+            cache_splits = 1
+        return max(base_splits, min(32, scratch_cap, cache_splits))
+    groups = batch * hk * triton.cdiv(query_len * (hq // hk), bm)
+    split_cap = 16 if seq_len < 131072 else 32
+    occupancy_splits: int = triton.next_power_of_2(triton.cdiv(512, groups))
+    return max(base_splits, min(split_cap, scratch_cap, occupancy_splits))

+def _refine_segmented_launch_config(
+    cfg: SegmentedLaunchConfig,
+    batch: int,
+    query_len: int,
+    span: int,
+    hq: int,
+    hk: int,
+    dim: int,
+    fp8: bool,
+    native_fp8: bool,
+    sliding_window: int,

+    if fp8 and not native_fp8:
+        return
+    if fp8 and dim == 128 and query_len >= 256 and 0 <= sliding_window < 255:
+        cfg["splits"] = 1
+        return
+    gqa = hq // hk
+    if (
+        dim == 512
+        and gqa == 8
+        and sliding_window < 0
+        and query_len >= 256
+        and 8192 <= span < 32768
+        and span >= query_len + 256

+        query_groups = batch * triton.cdiv(query_len * gqa, cfg["bm"])
+        if query_groups * cfg["splits"] < 96:

+            scratch_splits = MAX_LONG_EXTEND_WORKSPACE_BYTES * dim // 128 // scratch
+            scratch_cap = 1 << (max(1, scratch_splits).bit_length() - 1)

+                cache_cap = max(4, cache_cap)
+            elif kv_bytes <= 64 * 1024**2:

+                min(2 * cfg["splits"], scratch_cap, cache_cap),
+            )

+        return
+    if dim == 64 and query_len >= 64:
+        cfg.update(
+            {
+                "bm": 128 if span >= 8192 and gqa >= 2 else 64,
+                "bn": 32 if span >= 8192 and gqa >= 2 else 64,
+                "bk": 64,
+                "warps": 4,
+                "stages": 1,
+                "waves_per_eu": 2,
+            }
+        )
+    elif dim in (128, 256) and 8 < query_len <= 32:
+        cfg.update(
+            {"bm": 32, "bn": 64, "bk": 64, "warps": 4, "stages": 1, "waves_per_eu": 2}
+        )
+    elif (
+        dim == 128
+        and gqa <= 2
+        and query_len >= 256
+        and span >= max(8192, query_len + 256)

+            {
+                "bm": 64,
+                "bn": 128,
+                "bk": 64,
+                "warps": 8,
+                "stages": 3,
+                "waves_per_eu": 6,
+                "prefix_fast": True,
+                "qk_pipeline": 3,

+                    "bm": 64,
+                    "bn": 64 if span >= 8192 else 32,
+                    "bk": 64,
+                    "warps": 8,
+                    "stages": 1,
+                    "waves_per_eu": 6,
+                    "pv_split": True,
+                    "prefix_fast": False,
+                    "qk_pipeline": None if span >= 8192 else 3,
+                    "qk_unroll": None,
+                }
+            )
+            if gqa == 1 and span >= 8192:
+                groups = batch * hk * triton.cdiv(query_len, cfg["bm"])
+                cfg["splits"] = max(
+                    cfg["splits"],
+                    min(32, triton.next_power_of_2(triton.cdiv(192, groups))),
+                )
+        else:
+            cfg.update(
+                {
+                    "bm": 32,
+                    "bn": 64,
+                    "bk": 64,
+                    "warps": 8,
+                    "stages": 2,
+                    "waves_per_eu": 2,

+def _select_segmented_kv_upcast(
+    cfg: SegmentedLaunchConfig,
+    batch: int,
+    query_len: int,
+    span: int,
+    hq: int,
+    hk: int,
+    dim: int,
+    sliding_window: int,
+) -> KVUpcastMode:
+    """Choose conversion for the selected layout and visible attention span."""
+    gqa = hq // hk
+    kv_groups = batch * hk
+    kv_bytes = 2 * kv_groups * span * dim
+    if dim == 64:
+        return "native1" if cfg["bm"] >= 32 and kv_bytes <= 64 * 1024 else "native4"
+    if dim == 128:
+        if query_len <= 2:
+            return "native4" if span < 32768 else "normal"
+        if (
+            8 < query_len <= 32
+            and cfg["bn"] == 64
+            and cfg["stages"] == 1
+            or cfg.get("prefix_fast", False)
+            or kv_bytes <= 64 * 1024
+            or query_len >= 64
+            and (gqa <= 8 or query_len >= 512)
+        ):
+            return "native4"
+        return "normal"
+    if dim == 256:
+        if query_len <= 2:
+            return "native4" if span > 1 else "normal"

+            query_len > 8
+            and cfg["bm"] == 32
+            and cfg["bn"] == 64
+            and cfg["stages"] == 1
+            and (gqa >= 4 or query_len < 128 or query_len >= 512)

+            return "native1" if query_len > 32 else "normal"

+            short = span <= 256 and kv_groups <= 4
+            if query_len == 2 and kv_groups == 2:
+                return "native4"
+            if not (span <= 2048 or not short and (kv_groups == 1 or kv_groups >= 8)):
+                return "native1" if span <= 16384 else "normal"
+            packed = kv_groups >= 16 or span <= 2048 and (span <= 1024 or hk <= 2)

+        if query_len > 32:
